subject: pathology
title: Patau Syndrome, Sex Chromosome Aneuploidies, and Microdeletion Syndromes

steps.tx: Meiotic nondisjunction of chromosome 13 produces a severe malformation syndrome characterized by defective midline forebrain development and organogenesis. Presenting characteristically with microcephaly, holoprosencephaly, microphthalmia, bilateral cleft lip and palate, postaxial polydactyly, and scalp cutis aplasia, this lethal autosomal disorder is **Patau syndrome**.
steps.say: Patau syndrome causes severe midline defects including holoprosencephaly, cleft lip, and polydactyly.

steps.tx: The most common sex chromosome aneuploidy in males features two or more X chromosomes alongside one Y chromosome, most typically with a 47,XXY karyotype. Hypogonadism, testicular tubular atrophy, azoospermia, tall eunuchoid habitus, gynecomastia, and elevated follicle-stimulating hormone characterize **Klinefelter syndrome**.
steps.say: Klinefelter syndrome is a 47,XXY aneuploidy presenting with testicular atrophy, tall stature, and gynecomastia.

vis.alt: Endocrine and genital developmental alterations in sex chromosome disorders
vis.caption: Endocrine and phenotypic genital alterations resulting from sex chromosome and steroid pathway defects.

steps.tx: In Klinefelter syndrome, hyalinization and progressive fibrosis of seminiferous tubules during puberty destroys Sertoli and Leydig cell architecture. Loss of inhibin B causes feedback elevation of FSH, while Leydig cell dysfunction produces low testosterone and elevated estradiol, culminating in **hypergonadotropic hypogonadism**.
steps.say: Testicular fibrosis in Klinefelter syndrome drives hypergonadotropic hypogonadism with elevated FSH.

left.title: Klinefelter Syndrome (47,XXY)
points: Male phenotype with small, firm, hyalinized fibrotic testes
Low serum testosterone with markedly elevated pituitary FSH and LH
Tall eunuchoid proportions, female hair distribution, and bilateral gynecomastia
Elevated lifetime risk of male breast carcinoma and extragonadal germ cell tumors

right.title: Turner Syndrome (45,X)
points: Female phenotype with complete absence of one X sex chromosome
Streak gonads with accelerated oocyte apoptosis causing primary amenorrhea
Short stature, webbed neck, low posterior hairline, and broad shield chest
High incidence of bicuspid aortic valve and coarctation of the aorta

steps.tx: The only monosomy compatible with live human birth arises from complete or partial absence of the second sex chromosome, yielding a 45,X karyotype in over half of cases. Manifesting with streak ovaries, primary amenorrhea, short stature, and cystic hygroma, this disorder is **Turner syndrome**.
steps.say: Turner syndrome is a 45,X monosomy presenting with short stature, streak ovaries, and primary amenorrhea.

vis.alt: Primary amenorrhoea and streak gonads in Turner syndrome
vis.caption: Primary amenorrhoea, ovarian dysgenesis, and streak gonads characteristic of Turner syndrome.

steps.tx: Cardiovascular anomalies in Turner syndrome represent the leading cause of premature mortality. Preductal coarctation of the aorta and bicuspid aortic valves occur frequently, and progressive cystic medial degeneration of the ascending aorta creates a lifelong predisposition toward **aortic dissection in Turner**.
steps.say: Coarctation of the aorta and bicuspid aortic valves predispose Turner patients to aortic dissection.

steps.tx: Contiguous submicroscopic gene deletions detectable by chromosomal microarray or fluorescent in situ hybridization produce distinct congenital malformation complexes. The most common human microdeletion involves a three-megabase loss from the long arm of chromosome 22, designated as the **22q11 deletion syndrome**.
steps.say: The 22q11 microdeletion deletes TBX1, causing defective third and fourth pharyngeal pouch development.

rows: Thymic Aplasia, Hypocalcemia, Conotruncal Heart Defects
Cleft Palate, Facial Dysmorphism, Cardiac Anomalies, Psychosis

steps.tx: Classic DiGeorge syndrome arises when the 22q11 microdeletion disrupts neural crest migration into the third and fourth pharyngeal pouches. Consequent thymic hypoplasia impairs T-cell maturation and adaptive immunity, while parathyroid aplasia causes severe neonatal hypocalcemic tetany and refractory seizures, defining the clinical triad of **DiGeorge syndrome**.
steps.say: DiGeorge syndrome features T-cell immunodeficiency and neonatal tetany from thymic and parathyroid aplasia.

nodes.label: Failure of 3rd and 4th Pharyngeal Pouch Development
Parathyroid Aplasia Causes Profound Hypocalcemia and Neonatal Seizures
Thymic Hypoplasia Causes Severe Cell-Mediated T-Lymphocyte Deficiency

steps.tx: Congenital heart disease in 22q11 deletion syndrome involves embryonic conotruncal septation defects. Inactivation of the TBX1 transcription factor within branchial arches leads to truncus arteriosus, interrupted aortic arch type B, and tetralogy of Fallot, clinically categorized under **conotruncal cardiac malformations**.
steps.say: TBX1 haploinsufficiency causes conotruncal malformations like truncus arteriosus and tetralogy of Fallot.
